historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission engaged Schubart and Friedman, architects, to plan the rehabilitation of Jackson Playground and its field house.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to rehabilitate Jackson Playground and its field house to Biltwell Construction Company.
The Recreation and Park Commission named the newly built baseball diamond at Jackson Playground for Tony Lazzeri and set its dedication for June 15.

The Recreation and Park Commission ratified a $12,750 architectural services agreement with Delp W. Johnson, Poole and Storm, architects, to design a new field house at Jackson Playground, Mariposa and Arkansas Streets.

Because the neighborhood wanted the existing recreation building rehabilitated rather than torn down and replaced, the Recreation and Park Commission cut the fee of Delp W. Johnson, Poole and Storm, architects, from $12,750 to $8,606.25.

The reconstructed field house at Jackson Playground was to reopen on November 20, 1980, with a formal rededication on December 9 at the annual Christmas lunch of the Handicapped Services Division, unveiling a plaque to Ed Kelly, the division's longtime head.

After three community meetings, the Recreation and Park Commission approved renovating the children's play area at Jackson Playground, divided by a low curving concrete seat wall into a tot area on the east and an older children's area with swings on the west, with a new southwest entrance.
